title: Protocols for predicting Sphagnum bogs distributional pattern in China
author: Mingyang Cong
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbtxinpn
materials: Obtain the map vector data and software. A 1:1000000 administrative regionalization map of China was downloaded from the National Catalogue Service for Geographic Information (http://www.webmap.cn/main.do?method=index). ArcGIS10.3 was obtained from the Geographic Information System platform developed by the Environmental Systems Research Institute company in the United States. MaxEnt 3.3.3 k software was obtained from the Princeton University website (http://www.cs.princeton.edu/~schapire/maxent/).

steps.title: Collect Sphagnum bog center points
steps.instruction: Gather longitude and latitude coordinates for the central points of Sphagnum bogs across China.

substeps.instruction: Consult 'Swamps in China' and 'Marshes in China' and extract occurrence data from literature.
Use Google Earth (https://earth.google.com/web/) for toponymal geocoding of records lacking specific geographic coordinates.

steps.title: Select environmental parameters
steps.instruction: Select nineteen bioclimatic environmental variables to be used in predicting the pattern of Sphagnum bogs.

steps.title: Obtain climate scenario datasets
steps.instruction: Acquire historical and future climate scenario data from the WorldClim database (https://www.worldclim.org/).

substeps.instruction: Ensure data were calculated by the CCSM model (BCC-CSM1-1) developed by the National Center for Atmospheric Research.
Apply future climate datasets to four combined scenarios: RCP2.6-2050, RCP2.6-2070, RCP8.5-2050, and RCP8.5-2070.

steps.title: Predict dynamic distribution patterns
steps.instruction: Use MaxEnt 3.3.3 k to model the potential distribution of Sphagnum bogs.

substeps.instruction: Import distribution and environmental datasets into MaxEnt 3.3.3 k.
Set parameters to default values, except for the jackknife test used to calculate the contribution rate of each environmental variable.
Repeat the operation ten times using cross-validation.
Output the ASCII grid layer with the largest AUC (area under the ROC curve) value (0~1).
Load arithmetic results into ArcGIS 10.3 for suitability classification and visualization.

Convert continuous suitability prediction results into a Boolean classification of suitable and unsuitable habitats using the sensitivity-specificity sum maximization approach for threshold selection.

steps.title: Calculate distribution area shifts
steps.instruction: Determine changes in potential distribution areas by comparing current and future models.

substeps.instruction: Model the current suitable habitat area.
Use future climate datasets to model and forecast future suitable habitat areas.
Cross-check future areas against current distribution to identify regions of (i) gains, (ii) unchange, and (iii) losses.
Calculate the area of the identified gain, unchange, and loss regions.

steps.title: Identify core distributional shifts
steps.instruction: Track the movement of Sphagnum bog distributions using a Python-based SDM toolbox.

substeps.instruction: Calculate centroids from historical distribution to future distribution.
Concentrate species distribution into an independent central point and create a vector file depicting the magnitude and direction of changes over time.
Observe distributional shifts by tracking centroid changes among different SDMs.

steps.title: Assess key environmental factors
steps.instruction: Evaluate the importance of environmental variables using the jackknife method.

substeps.instruction: Create a series of new models by using a variable or excluding a variable in turn.
Compare model results to regularized training data.
Test gains and differences in AUC values among the models to assess variable importance.
